rationale: The single-bit reg round_key_update gates one combined if-block that drives ~384 bit-positions across key_mem_new/key_mem_we (128b) and prev_key0_new/prev_key0_we/prev_key1_new/prev_key1_we (256b), forcing one control net to fan out to hundreds of select inputs, matching the reported 300-fanout nor4 on the critical path. Splitting it into two buffer-duplicated copies (round_key_update_km, round_key_update_pk) and duplicating the small case-select logic so each copy independently gates only its own register group halves the load per net, letting synthesis size/place two smaller fanout trees instead of one oversized one, directly shortening the reported path through _07883_/_07893_/_08792_. Every assignment produces the exact same value on every cycle for every input (state, flops, and interface are all unchanged), so this is a pure combinational restructuring, not a functional change.
